column5: Fructan. Top bacterial fuel AND classic IBS trigger. Chicory, jerusalem artichoke, onion, garlic.
Fructo-oligosaccharide; shorter-chain fructan, distinct from inulin. Onion, garlic, asparagus.
Galacto-oligosaccharide. Legumes and some dairy. A FODMAP trigger.
Resistant starch, native granular form. Green banana, raw potato starch, legumes. Slow, distal fermentation (reaches the deep/under-fed colon) — hence "gentle" on the speed axis.
Retrograded resistant starch, formed when cooked starch is cooled. Cooled rice and potato. Slow, distal fermentation — "gentle" on the speed axis.
Soluble, gentle, gel-forming. Apple, citrus, carrot. Feeds butyrate producers.
Soluble fiber of oats, barley and mushrooms. Feeds propionate producers; lowers cholesterol.
Major fiber of whole wheat, rye and bran. Commonly overlooked; feeds Base Layer and Appetite Crew.
Husk fiber. Poorly fermented, so it bulks mechanically rather than feeding much.
Gel fiber of chia, flax and okra. Fermentable; soothes and feeds butyrate producers.
Polyol (the P in FODMAP). Stone fruits (plum, prune, cherry, apricot), apple, pear. Osmotic and fast-fermenting.
Polyol. Mushrooms, cauliflower, celery. Osmotic and fast-fermenting.
